word: My biological mother found out later that my mother had never graduated from college, and that my father had never graduated from high school.
meaning: 我的親生母親後來發現，我的（養）母從未讀完大學，而我的（養）父也從未高中畢業。
example: She later learned that his adoptive parents did not have the college degrees she had required.
hint:
中文解釋：親生母親的收養條件被打破，她得知養父母的學歷不符合她的要求。
1) biological mother (n.): 親生母親；syn: birth mother; ant: adoptive mother
2) graduated (v.): 畢業；syn: finished school; ant: dropped out
pronunciation: Emphasis: bi-o-LOG-i-cal | NEV-er GRAD-u-a-ted | from COL-lege / HIGH school.

word: She refused to sign the final adoption papers.
meaning: 她拒絕簽署最終的收養文件。
example: She would not agree to complete the adoption process.
hint:
中文解釋：親生母親因學歷問題而拒絕完成收養手續，形成緊張局面。
1) refused (v.): 拒絕；syn: declined; ant: agreed
2) adoption papers (n.): 收養文件；syn: legal documents; ant: rejection notice
pronunciation: Short + firm: She re-FUSED | to SIGN | the fi-nal a-DOP-tion PA-pers.

word: She only relented a few months later, when my parents promised that I would go to college.
meaning: 幾個月後，在我的父母承諾我一定會上大學之後，她才終於讓步。
example: She finally changed her mind after his parents made a promise about his future education.
hint:
中文解釋：親生母親最後鬆口，但條件是養父母保證孩子將來一定會念大學。
1) relented (v.): 讓步、軟化；syn: gave in; ant: stood firm
2) promised (v.): 承諾；syn: guaranteed; ant: refused
pronunciation: Soft: She ON-ly re-LEN-ted | a FEW MONTHS LA-ter | when my PAR-ents PROM-ised.

word: This was the start in my life.
example: This promise marked the very beginning of his life's story.
hint:
中文解釋：簡短有力地總結整個收養過程，呼應「人生起點」這個主題。
1) start (n.): 起點、開端；syn: beginning; ant: end
2) in my life (phr.): 在我的人生中；syn: in my story; ant: (n/a)
pronunciation: Deliberate: This WAS | the START | in my LIFE. (slow, meaningful)

word: And 17 years later I did go to college.
meaning: 十七年後，我確實去上了大學。
example: True to the promise, he enrolled in college seventeen years later.
hint:
中文解釋：呼應父母的承諾，17年後真的去唸大學了。
1) 17 years later (phr.): 十七年後；syn: after seventeen years; ant: immediately
2) did go (v.): 確實去了（強調語氣）；syn: actually attended; ant: never went
pronunciation: Confirming tone: And SEV-en-TEEN YEARS LA-ter | I DID go to COL-lege.

word: But I naively chose a college that was almost as expensive as Stanford.
meaning: 但我天真地選了一所學費幾乎和史丹佛一樣昂貴的大學。
example: Without thinking carefully, he picked a college with very high tuition fees.
hint:
中文解釋：帶點自嘲的語氣，說自己當時太天真，沒想清楚學費的問題。
1) naively (adv.): 天真地；syn: without thinking; ant: wisely
2) expensive (adj.): 昂貴的；syn: costly; ant: affordable
pronunciation: Self-mocking: I nai-IVE-ly CHOSE | al-MOST as ex-PEN-sive as STAN-ford.

word: And all of my working class parents' savings were being spent on my college tuition.
meaning: 而我那勞工階層的父母所有的積蓄，都在用來支付我的大學學費。
example: His parents, who were not wealthy, used all their savings to pay for his education.
hint:
中文解釋：強調父母的犧牲，點出讓他後來選擇退學的愧疚感來源。
1) working class (n.): 勞工階層；syn: blue-collar; ant: upper class
2) tuition (n.): 學費；syn: school fees; ant: scholarship
pronunciation: Heavy: WORK-ing CLASS | SAV-ings | SPENT on my COL-lege TUI-tion.

word: After six months, I couldn't see the value in it.
meaning: 六個月後，我看不到這樣做有什麼價值。
example: Half a year in, he felt the college experience was not worth the cost.
hint:
中文解釋：讀了半年，他開始質疑繼續讀書的意義，為下一步退學做鋪墊。
1) value (n.): 價值；syn: worth; ant: worthlessness
2) couldn't see (phr.): 看不到、理解不了；syn: failed to find; ant: clearly saw
pronunciation: Reflective: Af-ter SIX MONTHS | I COULDN'T see | the VAL-ue IN it.
